text.p: Gustavo Kuerten of Brazil won the French Open men's title by beating Spain's Sergi Bruguera in straight sets in Sunday's final.
Kuerten, ranked 66th in the world, beat 16th seed Bruguera 6-3 6-4 6-2 to become the first Brazilian to win a grand slam tournament.
Kuerten, the first unseeded player to win the French Open since Swede Mats Wilander in 1982, collected $695,500.
Bruguera, seeking a third triumph on the Paris clay after 1993 and 1994, earned $348,000.
Kuerten had impressed in previous rounds with wins over Austrian Thomas Muster, Ukraine's Andrei Medvedev and holder Yevgeny Kafelnikov of Russia.
He dictated the one-sided final with a huge variety of shots.
